clue.text: Act weakly to have debts seized by creditor

indicators.note: something seized by another is held within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for creditor
to have debts is to owe

explanation.surface: Someone shows weakness when a creditor grabs what they owe.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe or shrink in fear is to behave feebly, acting weakly in the face of a threat.

clue.text: Like in Le Monde, new setter makes a start

parts.note: Le Monde is a French newspaper, and the French for like is comme
cement is a setter, something that sets hard

explanation.surface: A crossword setter writing for a French paper gets going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' pretends to be the crossword compiler but is a substance that sets.
explanation.definitionFit: A beginning or opening is a start; the word is also used for a graduation ceremony.

clue.text: Place to plant hit in stomach — it hurts to fight

parts.note: to wind someone is to knock the breath out of them with a blow to the stomach
OW is what you say when it hurts
to box is to fight with the fists

explanation.surface: A boxer takes a body blow that hurts, at the place where the fight is planted.
explanation.definitionFit: A container on a window ledge in which flowers are grown is a spot for planting.

clue.text: Prompt on day off

parts.note: RE means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of day are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone is punctual even on their day off.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt in the sense of quick and willing, prepared to act at once.

clue.text: A short stretch of time criminal tries to reduce gradually

indicators.note: short means cut down, so the word loses its tail, leaving the familiar clipped form

parts.note: a moment is a brief stretch of time

indicators.note: criminal means wrong or bent, so the letters of tries are rearranged

explanation.surface: A criminal does a brief stretch in prison and tries to reduce his sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stretch' suggests a jail term, but it is just a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay off a debt in instalments or write down an asset's value over time is to lessen it bit by bit.

clue.text: Winners the night before occupying high chairs

indicators.note: a piece occupying another sits inside it
high as in intoxicated, so the letters of chairs are jumbled

parts.note: eve is the evening before an occasion

explanation.surface: Champions sit in high chairs the night before a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Successful people who attain their goals are winners in life.

clue.text: Removed head of pointless flower

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: something pointless is of no use

explanation.surface: A gardener beheads a useless flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' gives the phrase NO USE, run together, before its first letter goes. 'flower' is crossword language for a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is an English river, and a river is a flower in the crossword sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Period when expecting conclusion from beat poet

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: a rimester (rhymester) is a maker of rhymes, a minor poet

explanation.surface: A beat poet waiting for the end of a period.
explanation.definitionFit: Pregnancy is split into three phases of about three months each, so it is a period of expectancy.

clue.text: Problem for all to see inflames back

indicators.note: back means going in reverse, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: to fan a fire or a passion is to inflame it
U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: A public problem stirs up anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Military slang for a chaotic mess or foul-up, hence a problem.

clue.text: Bedlam, perhaps, in a little shop man's running

indicators.note: running as in out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's reads as is, linking the fodder to running, so only man supplies letters

explanation.surface: Chaos in a small shop where the shopkeeper is rushing around.
explanation.walkthrough: Bedlam was the popular name for Bethlem Royal Hospital in London, an asylum.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethlem asylum is an example of a psychiatric institution, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Rides boats, dropping ecstasy with miscreants

indicators.note: dropping means losing a piece, so a letter goes

parts.note: ferries are passenger boats
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
heels are cads or scoundrels

explanation.surface: Someone takes boat trips, giving up drugs, in bad company.
explanation.definitionFit: Big revolving fairground attractions with passenger cars are rides at a funfair.

clue.text: Jaguars welcoming care of species

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car
c/o, CO, is the abbreviation for care of on an address

explanation.surface: Big cats take care of their own kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguars' looks like the animals but means the cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A population of a species adapted to a particular environment is a kind or variety of organism.

clue.text: Take on inspiring role in puzzle

parts.note: to take on a part is to be it
a muse is someone whose role is to inspire an artist

explanation.surface: An actor takes an inspiring part in a crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: To bewilder or confuse someone is to puzzle them.

clue.text: Camp role models for foreign gentleman

parts.note: a camp in the sense of a faction or clique is a cabal

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters of role are reshaped

explanation.surface: A camp performer plays a part that will be a role model.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish word for a gentleman or knight, a man of good breeding abroad.

clue.text: Boris welcoming newspaper spin? I see what you're saying

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the other pieces go inside

parts.note: Boris Johnson was the leader, the prime minister
the i is a British newspaper, also short for the Independent
PR, public relations, is the trade of spin

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson takes a newspaper's spin and sees what is being said.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaf person who follows speech by watching mouths could say they see your words.

clue.text: Soothe suffering, maintaining light touch? This therapist might

definitions.text: Soothe suffering, maintaining light touch? This therapist might

indicators.note: maintaining in the sense of holding, so the other piece sits inside
suffering means in a bad way, so the letters of soothe are disturbed

parts.note: a pat is a light touch with the hand

explanation.surface: A practitioner who eases pain with a gentle hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is the wordplay, and the whole clue describes what the therapist does.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner who manipulates bones and joints by hand to ease pain is a therapist.

clue.text: Possessive person who'll succeed on time

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it

parts.note: an heir will succeed to a title or estate

explanation.surface: A possessive heir apparent waits his time.
explanation.definitionFit: A possessive determiner, as in 'belonging to them'.

clue.text: Settled close around fort

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other, holding it inside

parts.note: the close of something is its end
a sconce is a small fort or earthwork

explanation.surface: The deal was settled near the fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: Snugly established or installed somewhere, as a person comfortably settled in.

clue.text: Error from Messi's header and team's back in the lead

indicators.note: a header is the top or first letter of a word, with a footballing pun
back means going in reverse, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals; the 's reads as is
a side that is up is ahead

explanation.surface: A Messi header goes wrong and the team is back in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'header' looks like a headed goal but means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A confusion or blunder is an error.

clue.text: Takes off bloomers after a day

indicators.note: one piece placed after the other comes second

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday
irises are flowers, things that bloom

explanation.surface: Someone removes their knickers after a day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests underwear and 'Takes off' undressing; they are flowers and mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone off is to mimic or lampoon them, which is what a satirist does.

clue.text: Does one steal money?

definitions.meaning: one who nicks, a thief, is someone who steals
British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone pinches cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a pound, and also one who nicks, a thief.

clue.text: Wine merchant stocks up kind of liqueur

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top
a shop that stocks goods holds them, so the letters are inside the words

explanation.surface: A wine merchant stocks up on some type of liqueur.
explanation.definitionFit: Creme de menthe and creme de cassis are sweet liqueurs, so this word names a type.

clue.text: Rings round? Rubbish!

indicators.note: turned round means reversed, read from the end

parts.note: two hoops are rings

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at a claim of rings going round.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss scornfully is to rubbish an idea, and the reduplicated exclamation does exactly that.

clue.text: Problem badly affected taps

parts.note: something badly affected is hit, as in hard hit
taps are marked C and H for cold and hot

explanation.surface: A plumbing problem has hurt the taps.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag or temporary difficulty is a problem.

clue.text: Unidentified composer of piano nocturne

indicators.note: of in the sense of taken from, so the letters come out of the words

explanation.surface: A piano nocturne by an unknown composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Anonymous, the attribution for a work whose author is not known.

clue.text: Journalism in the Guardian, but not in Times or Sun?

definitions.text: Journalism in the Guardian, but not in Times or Sun?

parts.words: Journalism in the Guardian, but not in Times or Sun?
parts.note: an editorial is journalism; also 'the' is the article at the head of the Guardian but not of the papers named Times or Sun

explanation.surface: A boast that some writing appears only in this newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The definite article leads 'the Guardian' in the clue but not 'Times' or 'Sun'; commenters read it as THE, the blogger as A.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's editorial giving the paper's opinion is its chief piece of opinion writing.

clue.text: Ditch soldiers, at first, to make savings

indicators.note: the soldiers go at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers
a trench is a ditch

explanation.surface: Soldiers dig a ditch to economise.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut down expenses is to economise.

clue.text: Spirits initially not seen — they may be here

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: shades are the spirits of the dead

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Ghosts unseen at first may be lurking here.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the Greek name is thought to mean 'the unseen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek underworld is where the spirits of the dead dwell.
